gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histopathologically proven diagnosis of glioblastoma prior to registration, by pathology report;

candidate_evidence.quote: The primary purpose of this study is to test the safety of Pembrolizumab and Temozolomide in treating recurrent glioblastoma and to characterize the effect of this treatment on the participants tumor and immune system

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Characterize the safety and immunologic/genomic/metabolomic effects of neoadjuvant Pembrolizumab and Temozolomide in recurrent glioblastoma.
Participants will receive one cycle of Temozolomide and Pembrolizumab prior to removing recurrent tumor, followed by three weekly cycles of treatment until progression.

role_evidence.quote: Pembrolizumab will be administered at a dose of 200 mg as an IV infusion through a freely flowing IV.
Participants will take Temozolomide pills at home at a dose determined by body weight. They will take the pills for five days every 3 weeks.

agents.drug_class_hint: oral alkylating agent; established GBM therapy

coder_notes: Single registered intervention 'Pembrolizumab and Temozolomide' split into two agent rows. Design is SINGLE_GROUP; the two registered arms ('temozolomide', 'Pembrolizumab') both list the same combined intervention and appear to describe the components of one regimen, so control_arm_from_other_arms = not_applicable. Pembrolizumab treated as the only investigational agent; temozolomide (5 days every 3 weeks, given to all) coded soc_backbone, although an adjudicator could view the neoadjuvant TMZ rechallenge schedule as established_therapy_experiment; either way pembrolizumab remains the candidate. Target engagement coded yes: stated immunologic/genomic/metabolomic effect objective with neoadjuvant dosing before resection of recurrent tumour and the primary-diagnosis tissue block available (paired tissue).
